comp__health_monitor.content: Health Monitor component provides a set of functionalities to verify the health of the system and its components. It includes monitoring deadlines, logic, and heartbeats to ensure proper system functioning.
comp__health_monitor.title: Health Monitor

comp__lifecycle_launch_manager.content:
The :term:`Launch Manager` is a component that provides a framework for
 managing the lifecycle of any processes in the S-CORE platform.
 It allows for launching, monitoring, and controlling processes based on
 defined configurations and requirements.
 As such, it is a central part of the lifecycle management in S-CORE and
 knows about the state of all processes in the system.

 It's foreseen ECU projects will need a custom state management to fulfill
 ECU-project specific requirements.
 The S-CORE stack will offer a framework to control application lifecycle,
 but will not specify the State Manager.
comp__lifecycle_launch_manager.title: Launch Manager

comp_req__launch_man__alive_failure.content:
The :term:`Launch Manager` shall forcefully deactivate a :term:`Component`
when an alive supervision failure is detected for it, without notifying the
:term:`Component` and without allowing it to perform any cleanup.
This is then considered as a :term:`Component Failure`.
comp_req__launch_man__alive_failure.title: Alive monitoring failure

comp_req__launch_man__aslr_support.content:
The :term:`Launch Manager` shall provide support for launching process with
:term:`ASLR` (Address Space Layout Randomization).
comp_req__launch_man__aslr_support.title: ASLR support

comp_req__launch_man__capability_support.content:
The :term:`Launch Manager` shall provide support for launching :term:`Processes <Process>`
with configured OS-specific capabilities and privileges.
comp_req__launch_man__capability_support.title: Process capability support

comp_req__launch_man__central_default_de.content: The :term:`Launch Manager` shall be able to centrally define defaults for specific properties for the set of executables.
comp_req__launch_man__central_default_de.title: Global process properties

comp_req__launch_man__check_dependency_e.content: The :term:`Launch Manager` shall provide a method to check if at least one dependency has been executed.
comp_req__launch_man__check_dependency_e.title: Condition check based on at least one dependency

comp_req__launch_man__comp_activate_tout.content:
The :term:`Launch Manager` shall consider the component activation
attempt as failed if a component does not reach its :term:`Ready State`
within the configured timeout in ``deployment_config.ready_timeout_ms``.
comp_req__launch_man__comp_activate_tout.title: Component activation timeout

comp_req__launch_man__conf_of_comp_ready.content:
The :term:`Launch Manager` shall support configuration of conditions that
shall be met before the component is considered to have reached its
:term:`Ready State`.
comp_req__launch_man__conf_of_comp_ready.title: Configuration of component readiness conditions

comp_req__launch_man__configurable_timeo.content:
The :term:`Launch Manager` shall provide support for configurable timeout
:term:`Interval` to wait for the process to be stopped.
comp_req__launch_man__configurable_timeo.title: Stop timeout

comp_req__launch_man__consistent_depende.content: The :term:`Launch Manager` shall reject an inconsistent definition of set of executables dependencies.
comp_req__launch_man__consistent_depende.title: Invalid dependency

comp_req__launch_man__cwd_support.content:
The :term:`Launch Manager` shall provide support for launching a process with a
given :term:`Working Directory`.
comp_req__launch_man__cwd_support.title: CWD support

comp_req__launch_man__dag_logging_contro.content:
The :term:`Launch Manager` shall provide the possibility to log the :term:`DAG`
in a human readable format, triggered via :term:`Control Interface`.
comp_req__launch_man__dag_logging_contro.title: Logging DAG

comp_req__launch_man__define_swc_depende.content: The :term:`Launch Manager` shall provide a way to define for each :term:`SWC` (Software Components), its dependencies.
comp_req__launch_man__define_swc_depende.title: Condition check for each SWC its dependencies

comp_req__launch_man__dep_based_startup_.content:
The :term:`Launch Manager` shall start a component only after all its
:term:`dependencies <Dependency (between components)>` have successfully reached their :term:`Ready State`.
comp_req__launch_man__dep_based_startup_.title: Dependency based startup order

comp_req__launch_man__dependency_visu.content: The :term:`Launch Manager` shall have the means to log the current dependencies in a format that can be visualized when requested.
comp_req__launch_man__dependency_visu.title: Configuration dependency view

comp_req__launch_man__detach_parent_proc.content:
The :term:`Launch Manager` shall provide support for launching a process to
detach from parent.

.. note::
    Detaching from the parent process is also known as creating a daemon process.
    **Use case:** There might be processes which need to continue running independently of the launch manager.
comp_req__launch_man__detach_parent_proc.title: Process detach from parent support

comp_req__launch_man__drop_supervsion.content:
The :term:`Launch Manager` shall provide support to dropping all surveillance
and failure reaction activities of :term:`Processes <Process>`.

.. note::
    **Use case:** When the :term:`Launch Manager` shuts down, selected :term:`Processes <Process>` can be kept alive to
    continue their execution without interruption.
comp_req__launch_man__drop_supervsion.title: Dropping process responsibility

comp_req__launch_man__failure_detect.content:
The :term:`Launch Manager` shall be able to detect :term:`Component
failure` throughout the whole lifetime of a :term:`Component`.
comp_req__launch_man__failure_detect.title: Component monitoring during startup

comp_req__launch_man__fast_shutdown_supp.content:
The :term:`Launch Manager` shall support fast shutdown by terminating itself
without considering the started :term:`Processes <Process>`.

.. note::
    Fast shutdown allows the :term:`Launch Manager` to terminate its own process **normally**,
    without waiting for the started :term:`Processes <Process>`.
    **Use case:** This is relevant when the system needs to restart quickly,
    so it shuts down the launch manager in ordinary manner, but ignores the child processes.
comp_req__launch_man__fast_shutdown_supp.title: Fast shutdown

comp_req__launch_man__fd_inheritance.content:
The :term:`Launch Manager` shall provide support for launching a process with
given :term:`File Descriptor` inheritance restrictions.
comp_req__launch_man__fd_inheritance.title: File descriptor inheritance support

comp_req__launch_man__force_rt_selection.content:
The :term:`Launch Manager` shall provide support for forcefully initiating a :term:`run target selection <Run target>`
via the :term:`Control Interface` by aborting any ongoing transition and removing any queued selections.

.. note::
    **Use case:** In emergency cases, transitioning to another run target should happen as fast as possible.
    E.g., transitioning to the :term:`fallback run target <Fallback Run Target>` should not wait for the
    ongoing transition to complete or even for queued selections to be processed.
comp_req__launch_man__force_rt_selection.title: Force a run target selection

comp_req__launch_man__launch_manager_shu.content:
The :term:`Launch Manager` shall support normal shutdown by terminating all
process in the dependency order.
comp_req__launch_man__launch_manager_shu.title: Normal shutdown

comp_req__launch_man__launch_parallel.content:
The :term:`Launch Manager` shall provide support for launching :term:`Processes <Process>`
in parallel.
comp_req__launch_man__launch_parallel.title: Launching processes in parallel

comp_req__launch_man__launch_priority_su.content:
The :term:`Launch Manager` shall provide support for launching a process with a
given priority.
comp_req__launch_man__launch_priority_su.title: Process priority support

comp_req__launch_man__launcher_exit_shut.content:
The :term:`Launch Manager` shall exit after performing shutdown operation by
stopping all the :term:`Processes <Process>` it owns in the dependency order when requested.
comp_req__launch_man__launcher_exit_shut.title: Launch Manager shutdown

comp_req__launch_man__lazy_check.content: The :term:`Launch Manager` shall check availability of executables in the filesystem only when the executable shall required to be executed.
comp_req__launch_man__lazy_check.title: Lazy check of configured commands

comp_req__launch_man__lifecycle_lang_sup.content:
The :term:`Launch Manager` shall support Rust and C++ applications to
report their :term:`readiness <Ready State>` via the :term:`Lifecycle Interface`.
comp_req__launch_man__lifecycle_lang_sup.title: Lifecycle Interface programming languages

comp_req__launch_man__lm_ext_watchdog_cf.content:
The :term:`Launch Manager` shall support configuring the :term:`Interval` of
the internal health check executions.
comp_req__launch_man__lm_ext_watchdog_cf.title: Launch manager external monitoring configuration

comp_req__launch_man__lm_ext_watchdog_no.content:
The :term:`Launch Manager` shall trigger a notification to an external
:term:`Watchdog` for each successful self monitoring test execution.
comp_req__launch_man__lm_ext_watchdog_no.title: Launch manager external watchdog notification

comp_req__launch_man__lm_ext_wdg_failed_.content:
The :term:`Launch Manager` shall not trigger an external :term:`Watchdog`
notification if an internal health check failed.
comp_req__launch_man__lm_ext_wdg_failed_.title: Launch manager external watchdog notification - failed test

comp_req__launch_man__log_timestamp.content: The :term:`Launch Manager` logs shall contain timestamp information.
comp_req__launch_man__log_timestamp.title: Logging timestamp

comp_req__launch_man__modular_config_sup.content: The launch manager shall provide modular configuration file support to configure process attributes.
comp_req__launch_man__modular_config_sup.title: Configuration file support

comp_req__launch_man__monitoring_process.content:
The :term:`Launch Manager` shall provide support for monitoring adopted
:term:`Processes <Process>`.

.. note::
    An adopted process is a process that was not originally launched by the :term:`Launch Manager`.
    **Use case:** There might be processes which are needed to start very early during bootup and
    are therefore launched by the system before the :term:`Launch Manager` takes control.
comp_req__launch_man__monitoring_process.title: Monitoring and recovery: adopted process monitoring

comp_req__launch_man__multi_start_suppor.content: The :term:`Launch Manager` shall permit an executable to be launched more than once.
comp_req__launch_man__multi_start_suppor.title: Multiple instance of executable

comp_req__launch_man__offline_config_val.content: The :term:`Launch Manager` shall have a means to validate the configuration offline.
comp_req__launch_man__offline_config_val.title: Configuration Verification tool

comp_req__launch_man__process_input_outp.content:
The :term:`Launch Manager` shall provide support to pass the output of one or
multiple :term:`Processes <Process>` as input arguments to another process.

.. note::
    This is a similar concept to piping in shell scripting, where the output of one process can be used as the input to another.
comp_req__launch_man__process_input_outp.title: Forward process information

comp_req__launch_man__process_launch_arg.content:
The :term:`Launch Manager` shall provide support for launching a process with a
given set of arguments.
comp_req__launch_man__process_launch_arg.title: Handling process args

comp_req__launch_man__process_logging_su.content:
The :term:`Launch Manager` shall provide support for logging process launches,
:term:`Processes <Process>` exit/recovery, internal tasks, and interaction with external monitor.
comp_req__launch_man__process_logging_su.title: Logging state transitions

comp_req__launch_man__process_rlimit_sup.content:
The :term:`Launch Manager` shall provide support for launching a process with
a set of system resource limits (rlimit) which are defined by the
POSIX-Standard (IEEE Std 1003.1). I.e. RLIMIT_CORE, RLIMIT_CPU,
RLIMIT_DATA, RLIMIT_FSIZE, RLIMIT_NOFILE, RLIMIT_STACK and RLIMIT_AS.
comp_req__launch_man__process_rlimit_sup.title: Resource limit support

comp_req__launch_man__process_state_comm.content:
The :term:`Launch Manager` shall have a means for the launched :term:`Processes <Process>`
to communicate a state, which represents the launched processes' internal state,
to the launcher.
comp_req__launch_man__process_state_comm.title: Process state

comp_req__launch_man__queue_rt_selection.content:
The :term:`Launch Manager` shall provide support for queueing a
:term:`run target selection <Run target>` via the :term:`Control Interface`.

.. note::
    **Use case:** Queueing a run target selection allows an ongoing transition and all previously queued and
    unprocessed selections to complete, ensuring that the system transitions in an orderly manner without
    abruptly interrupting ongoing processes.
comp_req__launch_man__queue_rt_selection.title: Queue a run target selection

comp_req__launch_man__ra_comp_failed_esc.content:
The :term:`Launch Manager` shall perform the :term:`Run Target` recovery
action if a :term:`Component` recovery action has failed or is not
configured.
comp_req__launch_man__ra_comp_failed_esc.title: Component recovery action failure escalation

comp_req__launch_man__ra_comp_failure_sw.content:
The :term:`Launch Manager` shall perform the :term:`Run Target` recovery
action when a :term:`Component Failure` is detected
and there is an ongoing :term:`Run Target` transition.
comp_req__launch_man__ra_comp_failure_sw.title: Component failure during run target switch

comp_req__launch_man__ra_comp_fallback.content:
The :term:`Launch Manager` shall support reacting to a
:term:`Component failure`
by switching to the :term:`Fallback Run Target`.
comp_req__launch_man__ra_comp_fallback.title: Recovery Action - component failure switch to fallback run target

comp_req__launch_man__ra_comp_reactivate.content:
The :term:`Launch Manager` shall support reacting to a
:term:`Component failure`
by reactivating the failed :term:`Component`.
comp_req__launch_man__ra_comp_reactivate.title: Recovery Action - component failure reactivate the component

comp_req__launch_man__ra_comp_replace.content:
The :term:`Launch Manager` shall support reacting to a
:term:`Component failure`
by stopping the failed :term:`Component` and then starting a configured
:term:`Component` instead.
comp_req__launch_man__ra_comp_replace.title: Recovery Action - component failure replacing component

comp_req__launch_man__ra_comp_stop.content:
The :term:`Launch Manager` shall support reacting to a
:term:`Component failure`
by stopping the failed :term:`Component`.
comp_req__launch_man__ra_comp_stop.title: Recovery Action - component failure stopping the component

comp_req__launch_man__ra_comp_switch_rt.content:
The :term:`Launch Manager` shall support reacting to a
:term:`Component failure`
by switching to a configured :term:`Run Target`.
comp_req__launch_man__ra_comp_switch_rt.title: Recovery Action - component failure switch Run Target

comp_req__launch_man__ra_fallback_failed.content:
The :term:`Launch Manager` shall stop servicing the :term:`Watchdog`
if the transition to the :term:`Fallback Run Target` fails.
comp_req__launch_man__ra_fallback_failed.title: Fallback run target recovery action failure escalation

comp_req__launch_man__ra_rt_cancel_trans.content:
The :term:`Launch Manager` shall cancel all pending and ongoing :term:`Run Target`
activations before running any :term:`Run Target` recovery action.
The :term:`Launch Manager` shall be able to detect :term:`Component failure` during runtime of the :term:`Component`.
I.e. after reaching its :term:`Ready State`.
comp_req__launch_man__ra_rt_cancel_trans.title: Recovery Action

comp_req__launch_man__ra_rt_failed_esc.content:
The :term:`Launch Manager` shall perform a transition to the
:term:`Fallback Run Target` if a :term:`Run Target` recovery action fails.
comp_req__launch_man__ra_rt_failed_esc.title: Run target recovery action failure escalation

comp_req__launch_man__ra_rt_sm_notify.content:
The :term:`Launch Manager` shall notify the State Manger of a recovery
action that results in a :term:`Run Target` activation using the
:term:`Control Interface`.
comp_req__launch_man__ra_rt_sm_notify.title: Recovery state manager notification

comp_req__launch_man__ra_rt_switch_rt.content:
The :term:`Launch Manager` shall support reacting to a
:term:`Run Target` activation failure
by switching to a configured :term:`Run Target`.
comp_req__launch_man__ra_rt_switch_rt.title: Recovery Action - run target failure switch Run Target

comp_req__launch_man__rc_file_state.content:
The :term:`Launch Manager` shall support a :term:`Ready Condition` that is
satisfied when a configured file path exists or does not exist.
comp_req__launch_man__rc_file_state.title: Ready Condition - File state

comp_req__launch_man__rc_lifecycle.content:
The :term:`Launch Manager` shall support a :term:`Ready Condition` that is
satisfied when :term:`Component` notifies the :term:`Lifecycle Interface`.
comp_req__launch_man__rc_lifecycle.title: Ready Condition - Lifecycle Interface

comp_req__launch_man__rc_os_state.content:
The :term:`Launch Manager` shall support a :term:`Ready Condition` that is
satisfied when the configured binary is launched.
comp_req__launch_man__rc_os_state.title: Ready Condition - OS Process State

comp_req__launch_man__report_failed_live.content:
The :term:`Launch Manager` shall support reporting the failed liveliness of :term:`components <Component>`
via the :need:`logic_arc_int_op__lifecycle__report_failure` interface.
comp_req__launch_man__report_failed_live.title: Report failed process liveliness

comp_req__launch_man__report_lang_suppor.content: The :term:`Launch Manager` shall support Rust and C++ applications to report their liveliness.
comp_req__launch_man__report_lang_suppor.title: Alive reporting programming language support

comp_req__launch_man__report_liveliness.content:
The :term:`Launch Manager` shall support reporting the liveliness of :term:`components <Component>`
via the :need:`logic_arc_int_op__lifecycle__report_alive` interface.
comp_req__launch_man__report_liveliness.title: Report process liveliness

comp_req__launch_man__retries_configurab.content:
The :term:`Launch Manager` shall support restarting the process
a configurable amount of times, if the process fails to reach its
:term:`Ready State`.
If no retry attempts are successful this shall be considered an
:term:`Component Failure`.
comp_req__launch_man__retries_configurab.title: Configurable amount of retries on startup

comp_req__launch_man__rt_activate_tout.content:
The :term:`Launch Manager` shall consider a :term:`Run Target` activation
as failed if the activation exceed the time configured in
``run_target.transition_timeout_ms``.
comp_req__launch_man__rt_activate_tout.title: Run Target activation timeout

comp_req__launch_man__rt_comp_dep.content:
The :term:`Launch Manager` shall provide support to
define a :term:`Run Target <Run Target>`
:term:`dependency <Dependency (between run targets)>` to :term:`Components <Component>`.
comp_req__launch_man__rt_comp_dep.title: Run target to component dependencies

comp_req__launch_man__rt_rt_dep.content:
The :term:`Launch Manager` shall provide support to
define a :term:`Run Target <Run Target>`
:term:`dependency <Dependency (between run targets)>` to another
:term:`Run Target`.
comp_req__launch_man__rt_rt_dep.title: Run target to run target dependencies

comp_req__launch_man__runmask_support.content:
The :term:`Launch Manager` shall provide support for launching a process with a
given runmask.
comp_req__launch_man__runmask_support.title: CPU runmask support

comp_req__launch_man__runtime_config_com.content:
The launch manager shall provide modular configuration files support for configurations coming from
`OCI runtime configuration<https://github.com/opencontainers/runtime-spec/blob/v1.2.0/config.md>`.
comp_req__launch_man__runtime_config_com.title: Runtime configuration compliance

comp_req__launch_man__scheduling_policy.content:
The :term:`Launch Manager` shall provide support for launching a process with
certain scheduling policy.
comp_req__launch_man__scheduling_policy.title: Scheduling support

comp_req__launch_man__secpol_non_root.content:
The :term:`Launch Manager` shall provide support to be started with security
policy as non-root.
comp_req__launch_man__secpol_non_root.title: Non-root support

comp_req__launch_man__shutdown_signal.content:
The :term:`Launch Manager` shall implement a shutdown by sending a SIGTERM to
the process. In case the process does not terminate itself, a SIGKILL shall be sent.
comp_req__launch_man__shutdown_signal.title: Shutdown signal handling

comp_req__launch_man__slog2_logging.content:
The :term:`Launch Manager` shall support OS specific logging facilities to analyze the early
boot sequence.
comp_req__launch_man__slog2_logging.title: Logging slog2 and file support

comp_req__launch_man__start_named_run_ta.content: The :term:`Launch Manager` shall be able to start a named :term:`Run Target`.
comp_req__launch_man__start_named_run_ta.title: Launching run target

comp_req__launch_man__std_handle_redir.content:
The :term:`Launch Manager` shall provide support for stdin, stdout, stderr
redirection.
comp_req__launch_man__std_handle_redir.title: Standard handle redirection

comp_req__launch_man__stop_order_spec.content: The :term:`Launch Manager` shall permit the stop order of non-dependent processes to be specified.
comp_req__launch_man__stop_order_spec.title: Coordination stop dependency

comp_req__launch_man__stop_process_depen.content: The :term:`Launch Manager` shall be able to stop a process when all it's dependents are stopped if specified in the set of executables.
comp_req__launch_man__stop_process_depen.title: Dangling dependency

comp_req__launch_man__supplementary_grou.content:
The :term:`Launch Manager` shall provide support for launching a process with a
given set of supplementary groups.
comp_req__launch_man__supplementary_grou.title: Supplementary group support

comp_req__launch_man__support_secpol_typ.content:
The :term:`Launch Manager` shall provide support for launching a process with a
given security policy.
comp_req__launch_man__support_secpol_typ.title: Security policy support

comp_req__launch_man__switch_run_targets.content: The :term:`Launch Manager` shall be able to switch between different :term:`run targets <Run target>`.
comp_req__launch_man__switch_run_targets.title: Switch between run targets

comp_req__launch_man__terminal_support.content:
The :term:`Launch Manager` shall provide support for launching a terminal or a
session leader.
comp_req__launch_man__terminal_support.title: Launching terminal

comp_req__launch_man__time_to_wait_confi.content:
The :term:`Launch Manager` shall offer a configuration of the time to wait before
SIGKILL is sent. In case "0" is stated, the SIGKILL shall be sent immediately.
comp_req__launch_man__time_to_wait_confi.title: Configurable delay between SIGTERM and SIGKILL

comp_req__launch_man__uid_gid_support.content:
The :term:`Launch Manager` shall provide support for launching a process with a
given :term:`UID`/:term:`GID` (user name/Group Identifier).
comp_req__launch_man__uid_gid_support.title: Process user, group IDs support

dec_rec__lifecycle__lm_alive_polling.decision: The Launch Manager evaluates alive notifications periodically rather than as they arrive

sections: Launch Manager Alive Monitoring is polling-based
dec_rec__lifecycle__lm_alive_polling.title: Launch Manager Alive Monitoring is polling-based

dec_rec__lifecycle__thread_pool_process.consequences: Process lifecycle operations are organized around a configurable thread pool
dec_rec__lifecycle__thread_pool_process.decision: The Launch Manager uses a configurable thread pool to start and stop processes concurrently

 |

 | The module consists of one or more SW components and will be qualified as a OoC.
 |
 | **3. Security Management Roles**

 +---------------------------+--------------------------------------------------------------+
 | Security Manager          | <link to Module's Security Manager assignment or name>       |
 +---------------------------+--------------------------------------------------------------+
 | Project Manager           | <link to Module's Project Lead assignment or name>           |
 +---------------------------+--------------------------------------------------------------+

| **4. Tailoring**
| Additional to the tailoring in the SW platform project as defined in the process security management guidance we define here the additional tailoring on module level.
 |
 | - Excluded for this module are additionally the following work products (and their related requirements):
 |   - <ISO SAE 21434 reference>: <work product/requirement> - <Argumentation why it is not needed or replaced by another work product or activity.>
 |
 | **5. Security Module Work Products**
 | One set of work products for the module and one set for each component of the module:

feat_arc_dyn__lifecycle__app_health_mon.content:
.. uml:: _assets/application_health_monitoring_dynamic.puml
   :scale: 50
   :align: center

The most important interactions are the following:

.. list-table::
   :widths: 10 90
   :header-rows: 1

   * - Sequence number
     - Description
   * - 001
     - :term:`Launch Manager` configuration for the alive monitoring of the `Monitored application` is parsed. This contains for example, what is the expected interval of alive notifications, how long grace period is given before failing to a missed (never received) alive notification etc.
   * - 002
     - Start the startup grace period timer to allow the application to startup, before timing out to a missed alive notification
   * - 003
     - The `Monitored application` is started. (To simplify, no startup checks drawn here)
   * - 004
     - The `Monitored application` instantiate and configure the HealthMonitor
   * - 006
     - Cyclic reporting aliveness to the monitor.
   * - 007
     - HealthMonitor waking up and checking if the checkpoint(s) have been called
   * - 008
     - Report aliveness to the LM's application specific supervision, observing the health of the HealthMonitor itself
   * - 009
     - Checkpoint sent, but not on time
   * - 010
     - Wake up and check if the checkpoint(s) have been triggered. In this case it was not, and thus actions 011 and 012 are triggered.
   * - 011
     - Trigger a failure event to the Launch Manager. This event allows the monitor react faster than waiting for the timeout to expire.
   * - 012
     - Additionally, triggering alive must be stopped
feat_arc_dyn__lifecycle__app_health_mon.title: Application health monitoring

feat_arc_dyn__lifecycle__crash.content:
.. uml:: _assets/launch_manager_random_crash.puml
   :scale: 50
   :align: center

The diagram shows a component crash during an active Run Target (outside of a Run Target transition).
The component can be configured with a recovery action that defines the reaction to a crash.
If a Restart Recovery Action is configured then only the crashed component is restarted, not dependent components.
If the restart fails, the next recovery stage is to execute the Run Target Recovery Action, i.e. activating the Fallback Run Target.
See :need:`feat_arc_dyn__lifecycle__run_target_failure` for reference.
feat_arc_dyn__lifecycle__crash.title: Launch Manager - Crash Recovery

feat_arc_dyn__lifecycle__ctrl_fced_act.content:
.. uml:: _assets/control_interface_forced_activation.puml
   :scale: 50
   :align: center

The State Manager queues Run Target activations for "Running" and "Full" state.
During activation of Run Target "Running", the State Manager sends a new forced request for Run Target "Off".
The Launch Manager aborts the current transition and initiates the transition to Run Target "Off".
feat_arc_dyn__lifecycle__ctrl_fced_act.title: Switch Run Target Scenario - Forced Activation

feat_arc_dyn__lifecycle__ctrl_que_act.content:
.. uml:: _assets/control_interface_queued_activation.puml
   :scale: 50
   :align: center

The State Manager queues Run Target activations for "Running" and "Full" state.
The Launch Manager will process these queued activations in the order they were received.
At first the Launch Manager transitions to Run Target "Running" and subsequently to Run Target "Full".
feat_arc_dyn__lifecycle__ctrl_que_act.title: Switch Run Target Scenario - Queued Activation

feat_arc_dyn__lifecycle__ctrl_start.content:
.. uml:: _assets/control_interface_startup.puml
   :scale: 50
   :align: center

During startup the State Manager registers an activation callback with the Launch Manager to be notified about future Run Target changes.
The State Manager can query at any time the currently active Run Target. During an ongoing transition, it will be informed that the system is in transition and no Run Target is active yet.
After a transition is completed, the State Manager is notified via the previously registered callback about the new active Run Target.
Queries for the currently active Run Target will now return the newly activated Run Target.
feat_arc_dyn__lifecycle__ctrl_start.title: Switch Run Target Scenario - State Manager Startup

feat_arc_dyn__lifecycle__lcm_shutdown.content:
.. uml:: _assets/launch_manager_shutdown.puml

When the Launch Manager receives a SIGTERM signal, it will initiate transition to Run Target `Off` which leads to termination of all components.
Afterwards, Launch Manager process itself exits.

For detailed Run Target activation sequence refer to :doc:`./run_target_activation`.
feat_arc_dyn__lifecycle__lcm_shutdown.title: Launch Manager Shutdown

feat_arc_dyn__lifecycle__lcm_startup.content:
.. uml:: _assets/launch_manager_startup.puml
   :scale: 50
   :align: center

In case of initialization failure, the Launch Manager fails to start.
Once initialization is successful, the Launch Manager activates the configured initial Run Target.

For detailed Run Target activation sequence refer to :doc:`./run_target_activation`.
feat_arc_dyn__lifecycle__lcm_startup.title: Launch Manager Startup

feat_arc_dyn__lifecycle__run_target_fail.content:
.. uml:: _assets/launch_manager_run_target_failure.puml
   :scale: 50
   :align: center

The diagram shows a failing Run Target transition from Run Target "Minimal" to Run Target "Running".
Component app1 does not reach its ready condition, even after all configured activation attempts have been
exhausted, which makes the whole transition fail.
The Launch Manager then executes the Run Target Recovery Action of Run Target "Running" and activates the
Fallback Run Target. Components that are not part of the Fallback Run Target are deactivated, components
that were never activated stay deactivated.
feat_arc_dyn__lifecycle__run_target_fail.title: Launch Manager - Run Target Transition Failure

feat_arc_dyn__lifecycle__sup_failure.content:
.. uml:: _assets/launch_manager_supervision_failure.puml
   :scale: 50
   :align: center

The diagram shows a component supervision failure during an active Run Target (outside of a Run Target transition).
For details of detection supervision failures, see :need:`feat_arc_dyn__lifecycle__alive_monitor_start`.
The subsequent recovery behavior is identical to the process crash scenario in :need:`feat_arc_dyn__lifecycle__crash`.
feat_arc_dyn__lifecycle__sup_failure.title: Launch Manager - Supervision Failure

feat_arc_dyn__lifecycle__watch.content:
.. uml:: _assets/external_monitoring_sequence.puml
   :alt: External monitoring static arch


.. list-table::
   :widths: 10 90
   :header-rows: 1

   * - Sequence number
     - Description
   * - 001
     - The configuration. (notification interval, startup grace period, etc.) Additionally, if a watchdog interface is used, the used interface name (eg. /dev/watchdog) must be configurable.
   * - 002
     - If the :term:`Launch Manager` provides a client library implementation, the library must connect and attach to the :term:`Launch Manager`
   * - 006
     - Check the internal status and trigger alive notification (007)
   * - 007
     - Send the alive notification to the external monitor. (UART/SPI/GPIO/etc.)
   * - 009
     - Watchdog to check if the notification fits the expected window
   * - 018
     - If the status check fails, do not trigger alive notification (or :term:`Launch Manager` has crashed)
   * - 019
     - If there is no alive notification, trigger watchdog error reaction
feat_arc_dyn__lifecycle__watch.title: Launch Manager Watchdog Interaction

feat_arc_sta__lifecycle__cfg_params_stat.content:
.. uml:: _assets/config_params_static.puml
   :scale: 50
   :align: center

The Launch Manager configuration is structured around Run Target and Component configurations.
Each Component configuration specifies how the Component is started, monitored, and recovered during system operation.
Components can have dependencies on other Components, collectively forming a dependency graph.

Run Targets are configured through Run Target configurations, which define dependencies on Components and other Run Targets.
These dependencies determine which Components are activated when a Run Target is activated.

The Launch Manager is configured with an *Initial Run Target* and *Fallback Run Target*. The *Initial Run Target* is activated when the Launch Manager is first started.
The *Fallback Run Target* specifies the Run Target that is activated if a failure occurs that cannot be recovered.
feat_arc_sta__lifecycle__cfg_params_stat.title: Configuration parameters static architecture
